_note: New this session (Session 32, Growth playbook Phase 1). Neither this file nor an ARCHITECTURE.md section describing it existed before this session — the task that introduced it referenced both as if already decided; per ADR-0030's protocol, built from the task's own explicit, unambiguous shape and flagged here rather than blocked on. Only companies POSITIVELY IDENTIFIED as unscannable for a real, confirmed reason go here — a company this project simply found no signal for at all (no recognized ATS, no confirmed block) is NOT added; see PROGRESS.md's Session 32 addendum for that honest 'genuinely unresolved' list, kept out of this file on purpose so it stays a record of confirmed reasons, not a catch-all for unknowns. Session 36: ForSight Robotics, AIR, and Quantum Art (added Session 35 for a real extraction-capability gap) moved back OUT of this file into companies.json — CustomAdapter grew the css_selectors strategy that closes exactly that gap, confirmed against real fetched data for all three. This file's design is for reasons that are true independent of this project's own tooling (a platform with no adapter, a real network block) — a gap in this project's own code is fixable, and once fixed the entry stops being accurate, so it doesn't belong here anymore. Session 37: 7->15 — 8 new entries, all from Wikipedia's 'strong likely-active subset' candidate list, all confirmed live (not from secondhand research alone) as genuinely acquired/absorbed-with-no-distinct-presence or actively bot-blocked. Real reminder from this batch: a Wikipedia category being 'strong likely-active' doesn't mean unacquired — several of these were acquired within the last year or two, after the category page was likely last edited.

unscannable_companies.name: Totango
unscannable_companies.reason: Uses Rippling's ATS product (ats.rippling.com / ats.us1.rippling.com observed as real network requests on the live totango.com/careers page) — not one of Workday/SmartRecruiters/iCIMS this session scoped, and not one of this project's 4 supported platforms either. No adapter exists for Rippling.

unscannable_companies.name: Namogoo
unscannable_companies.reason: The real careers page (namogoo.com/careers) is behind an active bot-protection JS challenge (Cloudflare Turnstile served via abtasty.com) — Playwright's real browser never reaches actual page content, it lands on a 'Just a moment...' challenge page instead. Not a robots.txt block; this is the page itself refusing automated access outright.

unscannable_companies.name: BlazeMeter
unscannable_companies.reason: This project's httpx client receives HTTP 403 from the site's own WAF on a plain GET of robots.txt itself, which — per ComplianceAgent's documented 401/403-on-robots.txt handling (mirrors urllib.robotparser's own semantics) — resolves to disallow-everything. Confirmed non-transient and client-specific: curl and a real Playwright browser both get a normal 200 with no disallow rules for /careers at all, at the same moment httpx gets 403 — a WAF fingerprinting this project's plain-httpx client specifically, not a genuine robots.txt restriction or a real platform-support gap.

unscannable_companies.name: Centrical
unscannable_companies.reason: Same confirmed finding as BlazeMeter above: this project's httpx client gets HTTP 403 on robots.txt itself (resolving to disallow-everything per ComplianceAgent's policy), while curl and Playwright's real browser are not blocked.
